open_points.subject: store failure classification
open_points.text: If the store refused that record
open_points.question: Does "refused" cover every failure of the store call that writes the cleanup-failed record, or only a particular refusal category; and what exact store outcomes belong to that category?
options: Every failed store call, including transaction, I/O, integrity and symlink failures
Only a typed store refusal distinct from other internal store failures
A specified closed subset of store failures
open_points.default_guess: Treat every failed store call as the condition.

open_points.subject: result propagated after cleanup-record failure
open_points.text: the caller's store failure is the internal error instead, answered and followed by the same end of the process
open_points.question: What exact result must each layer return when cleanup is unconfirmed and its record cannot be stored: an ordinary internal_error, stop_required carrying an internal-error cause, or a result containing both internal_error and an explicit must-stop indication; and which module owns the stop?
options: Return ordinary internal_error and rely on the global rule that every answered internal_error stops the process
Return stop_required with the store failure as its cause
Return a composite internal_error plus an explicit must-stop flag
open_points.default_guess: Return ordinary internal_error and have surface stop after answering it.

open_points.subject: retry of an unrecorded sandbox execution
open_points.text: and the next start executes the element again
open_points.question: Which sandbox executions are automatically repeated at the next start: only function elements of durable runs, or also TrialExecutions performed by explicit try and admission; if trials are included, what durable record identifies the interrupted request, implementation, cases and actor to replay?
options: Repeat only a function element belonging to a recoverable run; explicit try and admission require another request
Automatically resume admission but never an explicit try
Automatically repeat every unrecorded sandbox execution, including explicit try and admission
open_points.default_guess: Repeat only function elements of durable runs; require a new request for try or admission.

witness.initial: An existing implementation and trial case can be tried explicitly, and no run is involved.
events: An agent requests an explicit try.
The store fails to write the TrialExecution.
The surface answers internal_error and the process ends.
outcomes: The phrase "the next start executes the element again" causes the trial execution to run automatically after restart.
A04 rule 6 keeps try inside its request and A14 startup recovery covers runs, so nothing reruns until an agent submits another try request.
witness.observer: The agent and anyone inspecting TrialExecution records see whether a new execution appeared without a new request.

open_points.subject: internal-error answer during startup recovery
open_points.text: answered and followed by the same end of the process
open_points.question: When the failed record write occurs while startup recovery is executing an element before the surface opens, is there no response and startup simply fails, or is "answered" intended to require some other externally defined startup error channel?
options: During a request, surface answers internal_error and stops; during startup, no response exists and startup aborts with an operator-visible error
Startup recovery opens or uses a response channel to answer internal_error before stopping
Cleanup-record failure is impossible during startup recovery
open_points.default_guess: Treat answering as conditional on an active request; during startup, abort before opening the surface and report the failure to the operator.

witness.initial: A stored run is running and has a function element with no concluded NodeExecution, so startup recovery must execute it before the surface opens.
events: The kernel starts and recovery executes the function element.
The store fails to write its NodeExecution.
outcomes: This passage requires module:surface to answer internal_error and then end the process.
A14 rule 5 requires recovery before the surface accepts a request, so there is no request to answer and startup must fail without an MCP response.
witness.observer: The operator and a client waiting for the MCP surface see whether the surface ever opens or produces a response.
